ov: A slender, medium-sized African wild cat with a small head, big ears and a golden coat spotted and striped with black. It has the longest legs of any cat for its size, and hunts by listening for rodents in tall grass and reeds, then pouncing.
rg: Widespread in sub-Saharan Africa; in North Africa only in Morocco, and reintroduced in Tunisia.
df: Mostly rodents (80–97% of its diet), plus shrews, birds, hares, frogs, insects and reptiles.

cf.tip: The caracal has long black ear tufts and a plain reddish-tan coat without spots.

fx: Its ears can rotate up to 180 degrees independently of each other.
It can stay motionless for up to 15 minutes, listening, before it pounces.
